About Covington County

Located in southeast Alabama, Covington County serves over 37,000 residents with a comprehensive court system. The county, bordering Florida and Georgia, combines rich historical heritage with modern judicial services to meet the community's legal needs.

Courts and Their Functions

Circuit Court

The Circuit Court serves as Covington County's highest court, handling:

  • Major civil litigation
  • Serious criminal cases
  • Appeals from lower courts
  • Family law matters (divorce and custody)
  • Property disputes

District Court

Operating as the county's court of first instance, the District Court manages:

  • Misdemeanor criminal cases
  • Traffic violations
  • Small claims up to $6,000
  • Preliminary hearings
  • Arrest warrant issuance

Specialized Courts

Probate Court

Focused on personal and estate matters:

  • Will verification
  • Estate administration
  • Guardianship appointments
  • Marriage licenses
  • Property deed recordings

Juvenile Court

Dedicated to youth-related cases:

  • Delinquency proceedings
  • Dependency cases
  • Child welfare matters
  • Youth rehabilitation programs

Treatment Courts

Offering alternative approaches to justice:

  • Drug Court: Rehabilitation-focused programs for substance abuse cases
  • Mental Health Court: Specialized support for mental health-related cases
  • Veterans Court: Tailored services for military veterans in the legal system

Covington County Probate Court

The Covington County Probate Court is responsible for handling legal matters related to wills, estates, and guardianships. This court also oversees the administration of estates, the appointment of personal representatives, and the distribution of assets.

The Covington County Small Claims Court is a specialized court that handles cases involving small claims, such as disputes over money or property. This court provides a fast, simple, and affordable way for individuals to resolve disputes without the need for a lawyer.
